spec_architectural_decisions.decision: flow-store.addNode REPLACES the existing trigger when a trigger-category node is dropped onto a flow that already has a trigger (preserve old trigger's outgoing edges + position; select the new node; undoable via the existing pushHistory).
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: createDefaultFlow() always seeds an undeletable trigger_start (flow.ts:448; FlowCanvas:118 blocks its delete), and the backend single-trigger rule rejects >1 trigger. Without replace-on-drop, customer_status_changed (and every other alt-trigger) is unusable on default flows. Scoped strictly to category==='trigger'; non-trigger node behavior is byte-identical.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: this is a deliberate single-trigger-slot fix, not a regression. It also fixes the pre-existing latent broken state for webhook/outbound/schedule triggers. Undoable (pushHistory). Do NOT flag as out-of-scope or as unexpected mutation of existing trigger behavior.

spec_architectural_decisions.decision: Catch-all is serialized as node.data.feature_group_id = '' (empty string); a specific group as String(group.id). The dropdown emits ONLY '' or a numeric string (free-text removed), so a non-numeric value is impossible by construction.
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: The shipped C3a dispatch job treats empty/absent feature_group_id as catch-all and a non-numeric value as a SILENTLY-skipped flow. Empty string is the backend-sanctioned catch-all (fgRaw.Length==0). Binding the picker to numeric catalog ids makes the silent-skip footgun unreachable.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: '' = catch-all is backend-correct (not a sentinel). String(id) keeps node.data a Dictionary<string,string> match for GetData('feature_group_id'). No free-text path exists.

spec_architectural_decisions.decision: Backend serves the catalog from the Invekto.Backend (BFF) service calling cxapi directly, via a new Shared WapCrmFeatureGroupCatalogClient + WapCrmFeatureGroupCatalogCache; Outbound is NOT involved.
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: Backend already proxies cxapi for the SPA (wa-templates -> WapCrmTemplateClient) and INMA (dynamic-fields cache). This is the sanctioned BFF pattern; the egress IP is already WapCRM-whitelisted in prod.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: not a microservice-isolation violation. Mirrors the live wa-templates + dynamic-fields proxies. WapCrmTemplateClient already lives in Invekto.Shared.

spec_architectural_decisions.decision: Process-wide IMemoryCache keyed by tenant_id only (wapcrm:featuregroups:{tenantId}); tenant_id comes ONLY from the signed JWT claim (ctx.Items[TenantContext]); single NSSM Backend instance; failures are NOT cached.
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: Mirrors InmaDynamicFieldsCache exactly (single-flight, CancellationToken.None fetch, Invalidate clears cache+inflight). No client-supplied tenant. Returned DTO is immutable.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: no cross-tenant leak — key is server-derived tenant only; no request body/query tenant override. Single-instance cache is acceptable (NSSM single instance); restart clears cache harmlessly.

spec_architectural_decisions.decision: Catalog response is TRIMMED before returning to the SPA: { id, name, selectionMode, features:[{id,name}] }. instanceIDs, rgbCode, sortOrder, systemKey are dropped. Cache TTL = 1h (Q final 2026-06-13, adopting Codex's recommendation + InmaDynamicFieldsCache parity) + a manual 'Kataloglu yenile' refresh button (invalidate+refetch) + a cache-invalidate endpoint.
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: SPA only needs id (picker value), name (label), selectionMode (text-mode disable), features (read-only over-fire explanation). 1h = dynamic-fields precedent + fresher config after a WapCRM reconfig; manual refresh further bounds staleness; ids are stable so cache invalidation is mostly cosmetic.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: payload trim is intentional (least-surface). TTL is 1h (the change was reviewed at 24h then lowered to 1h per Codex's own suggestion in a follow-up commit); not an oversight.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Single-trigger slot rule: flow-store.addNode, when a trigger-category node is dropped onto a flow that already has a trigger node, REPLACES the existing trigger (removes old, adds new at old position, re-points edges whose source was the old trigger to the new node, selects the new node) so the flow always has exactly one trigger and stays saveable. Undoable via pushHistory. Non-trigger drops are byte-identical to today. Verified by: dropping customer_status_changed onto a fresh (trigger_start-seeded) flow yields a single customer_status_changed trigger wired to the body.

Over-fire clarity: when a specific (non-catch-all) group is selected, the property panel shows a read-only list of that group's statuses (features[].name) with copy stating the trigger fires on ANY change within the group and that individual statuses cannot be selected. selectionMode is typed (1|2|3) with unknown modes failing closed (non-selectable); missing features[]/empty arrays are guarded.

error_handling.silent_failure_explanation: The catalog cache deliberately does NOT swallow fetch errors (mirrors InmaDynamicFieldsCache) — the Backend proxy maps them to coded 503/502/429 so the UI distinguishes not-configured (422) from fetch-fail. The only intentional 'silent' path is by design and safe: an empty/omitted feature_group_id means catch-all (documented, fires on any group change), and a non-numeric value is made IMPOSSIBLE because the picker binds to numeric catalog ids (free-text input removed per Q decision). Text-mode groups that could never fire a specific match are shown disabled, eliminating the silent-never-fires footgun.
